pretRelation.introTitre: Am I ready for a new relationship?
pretRelation.introTexte: Twenty questions about your ex, your evenings and what you expect from someone. Some weigh more than others. Answer the way things are, not the way you'd like them to be.
pretRelation.q1: When you think about your ex, what comes up?
pretRelation.q1a: Not much, it feels far away now.
pretRelation.q1b: A bit of nostalgia, and then it passes.
pretRelation.q1c: Anger or sadness, still very much alive.
pretRelation.q1d: The urge to get back in touch.
pretRelation.q2: Do you understand what happened in your last relationship?
pretRelation.q2a: Yes, my part as well as theirs.
pretRelation.q2b: Mostly, there are still some blurry areas.
pretRelation.q2c: I know what they did, not what I did.
pretRelation.q2d: No, I still don't get it.
pretRelation.q3: Your single life, right now, how does it feel?
pretRelation.q3c: Empty, I'm going round in circles.
pretRelation.q4a: Because I want to share, not because something is missing.
pretRelation.q4b: Because everyone around me is in a couple.
pretRelation.q4c: So I'm not alone in the evenings anymore.
pretRelation.q4d: To show my ex I've moved on.
pretRelation.q5: When you like someone, what do you do?
pretRelation.q5a: I go towards them, without rushing.
pretRelation.q5b: I wait to see if it comes from them.
pretRelation.q5c: I dive in, very fast, and get carried away.
pretRelation.q5d: I cut it off before it starts.
pretRelation.q6: Do you compare new people to your ex?
pretRelation.q6b: Sometimes, when a detail reminds me.
pretRelation.q6c: Often, and the comparison goes their way.
pretRelation.q6d: All the time. Nobody measures up.
pretRelation.q7: An evening alone at home, on a Friday:
pretRelation.q7b: Depends on the week I've had.
pretRelation.q7c: I look for someone to call, anyone.
pretRelation.q7d: I spend it watching what other people are doing on my phone.
pretRelation.q8: What you expect from a partner, today:
pretRelation.q8a: To build something, while keeping my own life.
pretRelation.q8c: Someone who fixes what's wrong with me.
pretRelation.q9: Your ex's things, photos and messages:
pretRelation.q9a: Put away or thrown out. I don't go back to them.
pretRelation.q9b: Still there, but I don't look at them anymore.
pretRelation.q9c: I reread them from time to time.
pretRelation.q9d: I look at them often, it does me good and it hurts.
pretRelation.q10: If a new relationship didn't work out, how would you take it?
pretRelation.q10a: It would be a shame, but I'd get over it.
pretRelation.q10b: It would hurt for a few weeks.
pretRelation.q10c: It would confirm that I can't do it.
pretRelation.q11: Your friends and family, what do they say?
pretRelation.q11a: That they've got me back the way I was.
pretRelation.q11c: That I still talk about my ex a lot.
pretRelation.q11d: That I've changed, and not for the better.
pretRelation.q12b: I'm working on it, it's moving.
pretRelation.q12d: Forgive? That would mean they were right.
pretRelation.q13: In a relationship, keeping time for yourself:
pretRelation.q13a: Non-negotiable, and I hold on to it.
pretRelation.q13c: I forget quickly, I blend into the other person.
pretRelation.q14: Do you have projects of your own, outside of love?
pretRelation.q14b: A few, a bit on hold.
pretRelation.q14c: Not really, I'm waiting for my life to start again.
pretRelation.q14d: My only project is finding someone.
pretRelation.q15: If your ex came back tomorrow:
pretRelation.q15a: No. It's clear and it won't change.
pretRelation.q15b: I'd think about it, but it would be no.
pretRelation.q15c: I don't know what I'd do.
pretRelation.q16a: I can talk about it calmly, like a chapter.
pretRelation.q16b: It's fine, but I'd rather avoid it.
pretRelation.q16c: It still makes me angry or tearful.
pretRelation.q16d: I can't talk about it at all.
pretRelation.q17: A first drink with someone new:
pretRelation.q17a: I feel like getting to know someone.
pretRelation.q17c: I spend the evening wondering what they think of me.
pretRelation.q17d: I do it to prove to myself that I can.
pretRelation.q18: What you don't want to go through again, do you know what it is?
pretRelation.q18a: Yes, precisely, and I spot it quickly in someone.
pretRelation.q18b: I have an idea, not very clear yet.
pretRelation.q18c: No, I keep ending up with the same kind of person.
pretRelation.q19a: It's back, sometimes higher than before.
pretRelation.q19c: It's low, I need people to find me attractive.
pretRelation.q20: When someone tells you "take your time":
pretRelation.q20a: I agree, and I take it.
pretRelation.q20b: I say yes, but I get impatient.
pretRelation.q20c: It annoys me, I've waited long enough.
pretRelation.q20d: I act as if I hadn't heard.
pretRelation.r1_d: Your answers pretty much all say the same thing: the break-up is still there, very close. You still think about your ex, you reread their messages, and new faces don't measure up. Single life weighs on you more than it carries you. That's not a flaw. It's what everyone goes through after a relationship that mattered. Getting into a couple now, most of the time, gives you a rebound relationship: someone who fills the hole, and who gets left as soon as the hole closes.
pretRelation.r1_a: Look after yourself first. Pick up something you dropped during the relationship, a sport, friends, whatever you like. Put away what's left of your ex, the photos and messages especially. And if the sadness doesn't shift after a few months, talk to someone whose job it is. You'll take this test again later, and the number will have changed.
pretRelation.r2_d: You've moved forward, it shows in some of your answers: life has picked up again, you go out, you may even feel like meeting someone. But your ex still takes up room. You compare, you haven't fully understood what happened, or you don't know what you'd do if the door opened again. A new relationship is possible, only it would risk being a threesome: you, the other person, and the memory.
pretRelation.r2_a: Finish what isn't finished. Write down what you've understood about the break-up, your own part included, and what you no longer want. It sounds like homework, but it works: on paper you can see what keeps going round in your head. You can meet people in the meantime, without committing, and without lying to yourself about what you're looking for.
pretRelation.r3_d: You're somewhere in the middle, and that's already real progress. The break-up is digested, broadly speaking. You know what you no longer want, you talk about your ex without your voice shaking. What's left is a doubt about yourself, or a slight rush: wanting it to happen quickly, to be sure it can still happen. You can absolutely start something, as long as you don't run.
pretRelation.r3_a: Say yes to meeting people, but let the relationship set the pace, not your impatience. A good test: after a pleasant first date, wait three days before deciding anything. If you can stand the wait, you're ready. If the wait eats at you, that's still the lack talking, not desire.
pretRelation.r4_d: Your ex is behind you, your life is full, and you know what you want. Very little is missing, and that little shows in one or two answers: self-esteem that's still climbing, a habit of forgetting yourself in a relationship, or an "I don't know" about what you'd do if it all came back. Nothing that should stop you. It's more a point to keep in mind for what comes next.
pretRelation.r4_a: Look at the answer where you hesitated, that's the one that counts. If it's time for yourself, decide now what you'll keep whatever happens: one evening a week, a sport, friends of your own. If it's confidence, let someone find you attractive without arguing. You can go for it!
pretRelation.r5_d: You've done the work, and it shows everywhere. Your ex has become a chapter of your life, no longer a wound. You've understood what happened, you've forgiven, your life runs without someone missing from it. And the wish for a relationship comes from the right place: you want to share, not to fill a hole. That's the best starting point there is, and it isn't that common.
pretRelation.r5_a: Don't put pressure on yourself because of it. Being ready doesn't mean the right person turns up next week. It means you'll know them when you see them, and you won't stay with the wrong one. Go out, meet people, and keep what you've built on your own: that's exactly what makes you good to be with.
